column1: # GE-T10's collision set: what rule 27 misread, and the German names the yes-or-no set lost.
# WHY. Rule 27's last-resort tier read German "Was ergab sich aus dem Versuch von James Lind?"
# as an English verification, by `was `; and the yes-or-no set lost two German subjects: "John
# Snows" names nobody (the German stemmer keeps an `s` after `w`), and "Hat Jenners Impfstoff
# vor den Pocken geschützt?" took `Pocken`, which the spelled pass finds before the stemmed
# THE RULES, DECLARED before a word of this set was written; scored first without them
# (`baseline.txt`), and not changed after a run:
#  28. a rule of `LAST_RESORT` in one language does not read a question `guess_lang` puts in
#      another; with no guess, it reads as before.
#  29. a German name in the genitive: when the question is German, the spelled pass also tries
#      each run whose last word ends in `s` or `'` without that ending (`Jenners` → `Jenner`,
#      `John Snows` → `John Snow`, `Semmelweis'` → `Semmelweis`). In the spelled pass, so the
#      name written first wins over a later one as any spelled name does.
# THE SET. Columns: qid, want, lang, question. `want` is the intent the question asks, or
# `none` for a question no rule should read and none should misread: scored as right when it
# is left unread (SMY-E468) or read as anything but a verification. The subject is the qid
# prefix's, as in every set, and is scored only on rows that want an intent.
# WHO WROTE THIS. The hand that declared the rules, after declaring them. Single hand.
